title: Deep pipeline optimized for high clock frequency
where_in_paper: Design goals / pipeline overview, often associated with the NetBurst or Hyper Pipelined Technology discussion
decision: Use a much deeper pipeline than prior IA-32 microarchitectures, reducing the amount of work per pipeline stage so the processor can reach high clock frequencies.
alternatives_or_rejected: The implicit rejected alternative is a shorter, higher-IPC pipeline that tries to do more useful work per cycle. The paper’s reasoning is that high frequency is a primary performance lever, and a deep pipeline is chosen to enable that frequency even at the cost of larger branch-misprediction penalties.
rationale: Shorter logic stages can be clocked faster. The paper presents the deep pipeline as a way to obtain large frequency gains, with front-end and branch-prediction mechanisms used to mitigate the resulting branch penalty.
outcome: The deep pipeline is presented as the architectural basis for the Pentium 4’s high clock rates, while the larger misprediction cost creates pressure for a strong front end and prediction scheme.

title: Execution Trace Cache stores decoded micro-ops
decision: Use a trace cache that stores decoded IA-32 instructions as traces of micro-ops, allowing the processor to supply already-decoded work to the pipeline on trace-cache hits.
alternatives_or_rejected: The conventional alternative is repeatedly fetching raw instruction bytes and decoding them in the normal fetch/decode path. The paper treats that conventional path as a front-end bottleneck at high frequency, though it may not enumerate every alternative implementation.
rationale: Removing repeated instruction decode from the common path reduces front-end latency and helps keep the deep pipeline supplied with useful micro-ops.
outcome: On trace-cache hits, the processor can avoid the byte-fetch and decode path, improving front-end bandwidth and helping sustain the deep pipeline.

title: Aggressive branch prediction to protect the deep pipeline
where_in_paper: Front-end / branch-prediction discussion, likely near the trace-cache section
decision: Use aggressive branch prediction and branch-target mechanisms, integrated with the trace cache, to keep the deep pipeline filled with correctly predicted work.
alternatives_or_rejected: Simpler branch prediction or relying on later resolution would be inadequate because the deep pipeline makes each misprediction expensive. The paper may not name a specific rejected predictor, but the trade-off is clear: a deep pipeline requires stronger prediction.
rationale: The deeper the pipeline, the more stages are wasted on a mispredict. Better prediction reduces wasted work and improves effective throughput.
outcome: The paper presents branch prediction as part of the mechanism that allows the Pentium 4 to maintain performance despite its deep pipeline.
